title: More Than $1 Billion in One Quarter: Why Did Alnylam Plunge 28%?
summary: Amvuttra surpassed $1 billion in quarterly sales, yet Alnylam cut its TTR guidance and lost 28% in one day. The reset was not about RNAi technology failing; it was about pent-up demand normalizing, revenue concentration and the timing gap before a second commercial pillar arrives.
source_status: Complete professional English adaptation of the approved public Drugnews Facebook/Dcard longform; argument sequence, financial figures, portfolio analysis, Taiwan implications, caveats and references retained

homepage_cover_image_alt: Amvuttra crossed one billion dollars in quarterly sales while Alnylam's growth expectations were reset
core_judgments: Amvuttra's commercial success did not disappear; investors reset the growth curve as pent-up launch demand began giving way to normalized patient flow.
Amvuttra represented approximately 86.3% of Alnylam's quarterly product net revenue, showing that the RNAi platform has not yet produced a sufficiently diversified commercial base.
The next valuation test is whether nucresiran can demonstrate incremental clinical benefit on top of modern background therapy and become a second commercial pillar before the timing gap widens.
